disease_label_per_paper: Acute bacterial prostatitis in an adolescent patient following blunt trauma
presentation_summary: 16-year-old male presented with suprapubic pain, difficulty urinating, hematuria, and fever four days after blunt lower-abdominal trauma from farm equipment.
Two days after the injury he developed fever, nausea, vomiting, dysuria, difficulty voiding, and blood in the urine.
Rectal examination showed a mildly enlarged smooth prostate with mild right-sided tenderness; suprapubic ecchymosis was present.
At hospital presentation temperature was 101.3 F, heart rate was described as elevated, and there was some hypotension; Foley placement at an outside hospital drained more than 600 mL urine.

CT showed enlarged heterogeneous prostate with extensive surrounding inflammation concerning for prostatitis with early abscess formation; labs showed WBC 18.67 K/uL, ANC 15.9 K/uL, PSA 15.2 ng/mL, and urinalysis with 12 RBC and 14 WBC per high-power field.
